criteria.evidence: All five guided sections plus Sources and Agent intent are substantive: What it does ("'Needs' says that another node must be done first ... the ready check ... reads it"), Inputs / Outputs ("Out: the error text is 'points at work' for a bare issue number ... 'not in the spine' for any other id"), dense Rules & behavior covering self-links, loops, bare issue numbers, schema versions 2 vs 3, nine Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and Out of scope naming fn-724, cap-718, cap-720, cap-721, fn-597, fn-726.

Items carry their why: "Every mix is allowed, because work across capabilities often needs a part of another capability"; "A loop is an error, not a warning, unlike a missing link. A missing link is a gap that the model fills as it grows. A loop is a link that exists but can never come true"; "The rename makes the field use the word of the ontology ... A reader must translate between the two"; "It gives a warning that names the old field, so an old model still loads."

Every section is discrete bullets; the function is stated as behavior ("The linter rejects a link that names work, a domain, a business intent or nothing."), never as a user story; acceptance is Given/When/Then ("Given a node that needs itself, or two nodes that need each other, when the linter runs, then it fails with an error that names the self-link or each node in the loop.").

Parent capability says only "'Needs' and 'identified by' (fn-725): the two links between capabilities and functionalities, and the check that each link points at a part that exists." The child adds the id-shape rule ("A link value that is a bare issue number, such as `725` or `#725`, gives 'points at work'"), the exact error texts, loop detection, the `depends_on` -> `needs` rename and the version-2 warning / version-3 error phases.

Terms are defined in place ("The spine is the file that lists each node and its links"; "the ready check (the script that tells if work can start)"; "the ontology (the written model rules)"), the what (two links plus the rename), the why (one field name with one meaning; links set order of work vs record origin) and the edges ("These links never go on work"; Out of scope with owners) are all stated. Minor residue only: the last acceptance criterion cites "#717, #722, #734" and "cap-742 and cap-747 still need cap-739" without saying what those nodes are, but it remains testable as written.
